main.description: A third-party statement vouching for someone else's CV record, written to the ATTESTER's repo and pointing at a record in the SUBJECT's repo. This is the answer to the problem every CV system has: self-asserted credentials are unverifiable. A co-author confirming an authorship claim, a supervisor confirming a supervision record, or an institution confirming a position produces a signed, independently hosted counter-signature -- with no central registry, and something ORCID structurally cannot do. Follows the id.sifa.org.employmentAttestation pattern: the strongRef pins the target's CID, so any edit to the target silently voids the attestation, and organisation identity comes from a ROR/Wikidata URI rather than a name string.

subject.description: DID of the person whose record is being attested.

target.description: StrongRef to the record being attested. The CID pins the exact version: if the subject edits the record afterwards, consumers MUST treat this attestation as void rather than as applying to the new content.

targetCollection.description: NSID of the target record's collection, snapshotted so a consumer can apply the right validation rules without dereferencing.

relationship.description: How the attester knows. A co-author confirming co-authorship carries different weight from a colleague confirming it, and consumers should be able to tell.

assertion.description: 'disputes' is included on purpose. An attestation layer that can only affirm is a reputation system, not a verification system.

entityRef.description: Wikidata Q-ID, ROR, or LEI URI of the attesting organisation, when the attester writes on an institution's behalf. Mirrors the id.sifa.* convention: never pin a free-text organisation name.

attesterRole.description: Equal language variants of the attester's role at the time.

statement.description: Equal language variants of an optional short comment. Not a letter of recommendation: this layer verifies facts, it does not evaluate people.
